stem: 3. Which of the following sets are equivalent or unequal or equal sets?
tamilStatus: pending original Tamil source transcription and independent editorial review

entries.question:
A = The set of vowels in the English alphabets.
B = The set of all letters in the word “VOWEL”
steps: List the distinct vowels: A = {a, e, i, o, u}, so n(A) = 5.
The distinct letters of VOWEL give B = {V, O, W, E, L}, so n(B) = 5.
The sets have the same cardinal number but different elements, so they are equivalent, not equal.

entries.question: C = {2,3,4,5} D = { x : x ∈W, 1< x<5}
steps: C contains 2, 3, 4, 5 and has cardinal number 4.
Whole numbers strictly between 1 and 5 are 2, 3, 4, so D = {2, 3, 4} and n(D) = 3.
The cardinal numbers differ and C contains 5 while D does not; therefore the sets are unequal and not equivalent.

entries.question: X = { x : x is a letter in the word “LIFE”} Y = { F, I, L, E}
steps: The distinct letters of LIFE are L, I, F, E.
Thus X = {L, I, F, E}, while Y = {F, I, L, E}.
Order does not matter in sets: both contain exactly the same four letters.

entries.question: G = { x : x is a prime number and 3 < x < 23} H = { x : x is a divisor of 18}
steps: Primes strictly between 3 and 23 are G = {5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19}, giving n(G) = 6.
The positive divisors of 18 are H = {1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18}, giving n(H) = 6.
Both sets have six elements but no matching membership lists, so they are equivalent but unequal.
